editorNote: Trust failing at different layers today: a certificate authority with single-byte keys, an extortion site allegedly run by someone paid to negotiate with extortionists, and a climate target quietly retired. Mistral and Google ship tools in the middle.

stories.headline: eMudhra's intermediate CA keys were single-byte numbers, crackable in under a second; Mozilla and Chrome are removing the root
stories.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme says private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were tiny values such as 4, 56 or 115, so at most 255 guesses recover one. Chrome and Firefox blocked the intermediates within hours of the Oct. 17 report, and Mozilla shipped an update removing the root on Oct. 20.
stories.whyItMatters: Browsers check revocation and Certificate Transparency, but Helme says curl, Python, Node, Go, Java and git trust CA bundles on disk and a forged api.stripe.com certificate was accepted in his test.

sourceLinks.title: Eight Bits of Trust: eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds - Scott Helme

stories.headline: Mistral ships Voxtral 3: transcription, realtime and text-to-speech models plus a voice-agent SDK
stories.summary: The family covers Small and Mini batch transcription (50+ languages), a realtime model with under 500 ms latency, and Mini TTS in 35+ languages. Batch transcription is priced from $0.0035 per minute, and Mistral's own FLEURS benchmark puts Small at about 4% word error rate ahead of Whisper large-v3.
stories.whyItMatters: The benchmarks are Mistral's own, and the page states no licence for the models.

stories.headline: UNEP: the Paris 1.5°C goal is no longer achievable; it now frames the aim as overshoot then return
stories.summary: The 2026 Emissions Gap Report says exceeding 1.5°C is imminent and calls for cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 versus 2025. Current pledges would deliver only 5–8% by 2030, and about 320 gigatons of CO2 would need removing by 2100.
stories.whyItMatters: It shifts the official target from avoiding 1.5°C to limiting overshoot and returning to it by century's end.

sourceLinks.title: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026: 1.5°C overshoot - UNRIC

stories.headline: Feds suspect a ransom negotiator ran ShinyHunters' Shinywire extortion site
stories.summary: Krebs reports Canadian security executive Edward Dubrovsky has been charged with extortion-related offences, and prosecutors want him held pending trial. Shinywire listed nearly 100 victims between May and October; the FBI says the group has extorted over $70 million this year.
stories.whyItMatters: Most claims rest on anonymous sources and none has been proven in court; other named people are not charged.

sourceLinks.title: Feds suspect ransom negotiator ran ShinyHunters extortion site - Krebs on Security

stories.headline: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a PyTorch backend for TPUs, at version 0.2.0
stories.summary: The Apache-2.0 repo offers custom ATen kernels, torch.compile integration, a compilation cache and data and tensor parallelism, with example Llama, Qwen and UNet models. It requires Python 3.11+, and its dependencies section is still marked TBD.
stories.whyItMatters: It is an early release that lets PyTorch code target TPUs directly, though the notebooks need a TPU VM.

stories.headline: Ofcom concedes it cannot collect every Online Safety Act fine abroad, per 4chan's lawyer
stories.summary: Ofcom chief Melanie Dawes told MPs 'we won't be able to recover every single fine on online safety'. Preston Byrne, counsel to 4chan, says a US court ruled against 4chan on sovereign immunity but suggested it would likely not enforce a UK judgment that violates the First Amendment.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a partisan account by 4chan's lawyer; Ofcom is expected to seek interim business-disruption powers to block foreign sites.
